clue.text: Here's good advice from roadshow, I tweet excitedly

indicators.note: doing something excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV presenter fires off an over-eager tweet full of tips after a touring show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ROADSHOW I TWEET are rearranged ('excitedly') into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a brief hint or warning offered to someone sensible enough to heed it.

clue.text: In deficit, uncertain what to do

definitions.meaning: selling ... means making less than it cost, being in deficit
being stumped or bewildered, with no idea how to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone in debt and unsure of the next step.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase has a commercial sense, trading below cost, and an idiomatic one, being perplexed.

clue.text: I'm on oboe an uncle composed for very rarely

indicators.note: a piece composed is put together, so the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician boasts of playing a piece their uncle wrote for the oboe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' signals rearranging I'M ON OBOE AN UNCLE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something that happens almost never, as seldom as a second full moon in a month.

clue.text: Redecorate at university after party

indicators.note: after places the university word behind the party word

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student plans to repaint their room after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate or refurbish a room or house is a colloquial phrasal verb for decorating it.

clue.text: Get damaged boat home

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in for the evening

explanation.surface: A sailor tries to bring a broken boat back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to acquire or come to possess something.

clue.text: Great number right inside city pub?

parts.note: a host is a large crowd or multitude

indicators.note: inside places the right abbreviation within the city name

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A crowd of people inside a city drinking establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or tavern is a dated, slightly jocular word for a place serving drink; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Bird wife precooked, for a change

indicators.note: changing them means the letters are rearranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A wife has made a ready meal to break the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: W (wife) plus PRECOOKED are rearranged ('for a change').
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-drilling avian is a kind of bird, the definition naming its class.

clue.text: One way that may get you into Hollywood

definitions.text: One way that may get you into Hollywood

parts.words: One way that may get you into Hollywood
parts.note: reads as a route to film stardom, but literally a famous road running into the Hollywood district of Los Angeles, and also a film about Hollywood

explanation.surface: Advice on breaking into the film industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous avenue in Los Angeles runs through Hollywood, so it is literally a way in; it is also a Billy Wilder film.

clue.text: Game girl doesn't finish

indicators.note: a word that does not finish loses its last letter

parts.note: Bridget is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl abandons a game partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDGET loses its final T ('doesn't finish').
explanation.definitionFit: A trick-taking card game for four players in partnerships.

clue.text: A nobleman catching cold in story

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A tale in which an aristocrat comes down with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative or report of events, as in giving an account of what happened.

clue.text: Famous Oxford don earlier than expected bringing page in

indicators.note: bringing something in takes it inside, here the page letter going into the word
in completes the phrase that places the page letter inside the other piece

parts.note: sooner means earlier than planned or anticipated

explanation.surface: A well-known academic turns up early with a page in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: William Archibald Spooner, warden of New College, Oxford, gave his name to the transposed-sound slip.

clue.text: Heading for Oberhausen with German miss

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Someone travelling with a German to Oberhausen misses something.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberhausen is a German city; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out or skip something is to miss it.

clue.text: Extra large meal that's all over the place

parts.note: in cricket a wide is one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat
a spread is a lavish array of food

explanation.surface: An oversized feast spilling everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, counts as an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found everywhere or extensively distributed is described this way.

clue.text: Person going round a London college with a cleaning agent

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the person word encloses the rest

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person
King's College London is a university college

explanation.surface: A student goes round a London college carrying a cleaning product.
explanation.walkthrough: King's College is part of the University of London; 'going round' wraps the person round it, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is widely used as a household cleaner as well as a raising agent.

clue.text: Remain briefly with convict in camp

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, dropping the last letter

parts.note: to stay is to remain
a lag is slang for a prisoner, usually an old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner told to stay in camp for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A German prisoner-of-war camp of the Second World War.

clue.text: Pot Republican placed in new cubicle

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the party letter goes within the rearranged word
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A cannabis-smoking Republican is found in a brand-new toilet stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CUBICLE to CUCIBLE; 'placed in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat-resistant vessel for melting metals is a type of pot.

clue.text: Join a bishop about to go inside for fish

indicators.note: to go inside places the following pieces within the join word

parts.note: a seam is a join between two pieces
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bishop is invited along for a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' looks like a verb inviting someone, but it is the noun for a stitched line; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine food species of the family Sparidae, such as gilt-head, is a fish.

clue.text: Traveller with tale about fashionable shopkeeper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pilgrim encloses the fashion word

parts.note: the Miller is one of Chaucer's pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales, telling his own story
in means fashionable, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A travelling storyteller recounts a tale about a fashionable shop owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'traveller with tale' is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims; 'about' wraps him round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker and seller of hats keeps a shop, so is a type of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Nonconformist male is in good health

parts.note: fit means healthy

explanation.surface: A dissenting man who keeps in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not fit in with others is an outsider who refuses to conform.

clue.text: Win playing Ulster

indicators.note: playing about with letters shuffles them into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports team beats Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is a province of Ireland, and an Irish rugby side.
explanation.definitionFit: A win is a successful outcome, which in football is called a good result.

clue.text: Set of questions about English politician causes violent disturbance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exam word encloses the others

parts.note: a test is a set of questions, an exam
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An exam on a British lawmaker triggers an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm, or figuratively a great upheaval or commotion.

clue.text: Look initially within for papers, bright in colour

indicators.note: within places that letter inside the word for
initially means the first letter only of the next word

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: Instructions to search for documents that are brightly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link here: it is taken as written and opened up by 'within'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flushed or ruddy complexion, or showy decoration, is vividly coloured.

clue.text: Kill beautiful woman, reportedly a ringer?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: to slay is to kill, and a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A murder of a beauty, as reported by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAY BELLE said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jingling bell on a horse's harness is something that rings; the question mark plays on ringer as a lookalike.

clue.text: Party in power losing face

indicators.note: losing face means dropping the front letter

parts.note: steam is a source of power, as in a steam engine

explanation.surface: A governing political group suffers humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: STEAM loses its first letter ('losing face'); 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A group working together, such as a search party, is a side or squad.

clue.text: Plan best left forgotten

indicators.note: forgotten means dropped, so that letter is removed

parts.note: ideal means best or perfect

explanation.surface: A scheme that would be better abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme of action, as in having an idea to do something.

clue.text: Irish individual keeping gold, metal extracted from this?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the number word holds the gold

parts.note: one means a single individual
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An Irishman keeps hold of his gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock from which iron is smelted is the raw source of the metal, so the clue is an &lit-style description.

clue.text: Socialist recording reveals time-consuming bureaucracy

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A left-winger's recording exposes slow officialdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official procedure, named after the ribbon once tying government documents.

clue.text: Comic mentioned bar ad for fruit machine

indicators.note: comic as an adjective means funny or absurd, hinting the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedian referred to a pub advert promoting a gambling machine.
explanation.walkthrough: MENTIONED BAR AD is rearranged ('Comic'); 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine for gambling, nicknamed for its single lever and for taking punters' money.
